arguments.content:
validator-fix-4: claimer cold-start liveness

Static review of fix/val-doc-1...task/validator-fix-4 · commit 52d00c9 · 2 files, +37/−1

TL;DR

The bounded Claimed-log scan can legitimately return no event after a fresh start or long downtime. Previously that produced null and stopped the claim decision. The patch now treats “no log” like a scan failure: it enters the existing indexer fallback, obtains the latest claimed state root, and can submit the pending claim.

Verdict: approve. The four-line production change directly repairs the described liveness hole, follows the established snapshot.ts pattern, and has a focused regression test. No blocking correctness finding was identified in the inspected diff.
  • claimer.ts
  • claimer.test.ts
  • Review verdict
  • Residual findings

What changed, by file

validator-cli/src/helpers/claimer.ts

Change. Imports NoMessageSavedError. After the bounded scan, an absent lastClaimLog is now converted into an exception; the existing catch then calls fetchLatestClaimedEpoch(veaOutbox.target, chainId). A found log still uses its data field exactly as before.

const lastClaimLog = await findLatestLog({ ... });
if (!lastClaimLog) throw new NoMessageSavedError(String(veaOutbox.target));
lastClaimedStateroot = lastClaimLog.data;

// Existing catch path:
const claimData = await fetchLatestClaimedEpoch(veaOutbox.target, chainId);
lastClaimedStateroot = claimData ? claimData.stateRoot : ethers.ZeroHash;

Why. Optional chaining previously mapped an empty scan to null without throwing. The later null guard returned before comparing roots, so repeated runs could silently skip claiming. The explicit throw deliberately reuses the indexer fallback already used for RPC/scanner exceptions.

Behavioral boundary. The change affects only the “scan completed but found no Claimed event” branch. Settlement gating, settled-block snapshot/state-root reads, successful log scans, and the final “snapshot differs from both current and last claimed roots” condition are unchanged.
